#1959. Tottenham given Harry Kane transfer hope despite Bayern Munich contract renewal (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 16:41, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 16:41

Harry Kane could be tempted by a move back to Tottenham Hotspur if he wins the Champions League with Bayern Munich, but under certain conditions, a former Spurs striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Kane is gearing up for a return to domestic football after breaking the England all-time men's appearance record during the November international break, in addition to scoring in back-to-back games against Croatia and Spain.

The 33-year-old also made headlines off the field recently by signing a new contract with Bayern to the summer of 2029, and he already boasts 20 goal involvements in 15 games for the Bavarians this season; 10 of his own and 10 assists.

However, speculation surrounding a possible return to Tottenham one day continues to linger, as the Lilywhites reportedly retain the right to match any bid that comes in from another club for their all-time top scorer.

Sports Mole recently asked Darren Bent about Tottenham's chances of re-signing Kane, and the ex-Spurs striker can see the England captain being tempted to go back to England, but only if the Lilywhites are competing in the top half of the table.

"We saw that new contract, which they were delighted about. The way Kane spoke, there was no real urgency to get back to the Premier League, but you never know," Bent said via MrQ betting site.

"If Bayern win the Champions League this year, then I guess he's ticked every box he wants to tick. He's won the league over there, and he's won trophies over there.

"He's won the Golden Boot. The big one would be the Champions League. If he could go over there and win that, it puts him in a different bracket, certainly over there, because you look at the great strikers Bayern Munich have had, they've all won the Champions League. Lewandowski, these types of players.

"I'm guessing that's the last box he's got to tick. If Kane was to go and win the Champions League this year, there's no reason why he couldn't then go, 'There's nothing more for me to achieve over there if I've won all the big trophies there are to win in Germany. Let me come back and see where Spurs are and potentially get a move there.'

"But then again, it all depends on where Spurs are, because there's no point in leaving Bayern Munich if Spurs are languishing at the bottom of the table, fighting relegation, or even in the bottom half of the table. What's he coming back for?"

When Kane departed Tottenham for Bayern Munich in the summer of 2023, he left with the second-highest goals total in the history of the Premier League, racking up 213 English top-flight strikes.

However, the striker left before he could either match or surpass Alan Shearer's unrivalled total of 260 Premier League goals; he needs another 47 to draw level with the Newcastle United legend.

During Kane's final year at Tottenham, Shearer expressed complete confidence that the Ballon d'Or winner would break his record one day, having been told of Kane's desire to do so by the man himself.

"I know how much he wants it - he's told me - which is fine, because I was exactly the same," Shearer said in an interview with the Premier League.

However, Kane then told FourFourTwo in September that the desire had 'diminished', so if he is to head back to his homeland, finally winning a trophy with Tottenham is likely to be his primary motivator.

Darren Bent was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of MrQ Live Casino.

#1958. Cruzeiro vs Palmeiras - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 17 Nov 2026 17:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 09:25

Cruzeiro will be looking to strengthen their hopes of securing a direct place in the Copa Libertadores when they welcome Palmeiras to Mineirao on Wednesday in the Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A.

The hosts have enjoyed a remarkable turnaround under Artur Jorge, climbing from the bottom of the table to third place with 60 points after winning their last four league matches, while the visitors remain firmly in the title race, sitting second with 73 points, three behind leaders Flamengo.

Cruzeiro's transformation under Jorge has been one of the most impressive stories of the Brazilian top-flight campaign, with the Portuguese coach overseeing a dramatic recovery after taking charge of a team that had collected just four points from their opening eight matches.

From the ninth round through to the 34th, the Foxes accumulated 56 points, a tally bettered only by Flamengo during that period and even superior to Palmeiras' return over the same stretch.

Their improvement has been particularly evident in recent weeks, with four consecutive victories providing further evidence of a side that has developed greater consistency and resilience when faced with difficult situations.

Cruzeiro demonstrated those qualities in their most recent outing against Bahia, recovering from an early setback to secure a comeback 3-2 victory.

Kaio Jorge was instrumental in the turnaround, scoring twice, while Bruno Rodrigues also found the net to complete an impressive result that strengthened their position in the top three.

With their qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores already secured, Cruzeiro's immediate objective is to guarantee direct entry into the competition, making Wednesday's encounter particularly important with two consecutive away fixtures to follow.

Indeed, Palmeiras arrive with an impressive away record, having collected 31 points from 17 matches on their travels, suffering just two defeats in the process.

The visitors also boast the league's strongest defensive record, having conceded only 23 goals, while their current 11-match unbeaten run in the Brasileirao underlines their consistency during the closing stages of the campaign.

Abel Ferreira's side were particularly ruthless in their previous league outing, producing a dominant first-half display to establish a 4-0 advantage before eventually recording a 6-1 victory over Remo.

Nevertheless, the visitors' demanding schedule could become a significant factor on Wednesday, having recently booked their place in the Copa do Brasil final despite losing 2-1 to Vasco da Gama in the second leg of their semi-final before progressing on penalties.

With Palmeiras still competing on three fronts, Ferreira must carefully manage his available resources, particularly with several players having only recently returned from international duty.

The title race also leaves little room for error, as Palmeiras cannot afford to drop points if they are to maintain pressure on Flamengo before the two sides meet on November 21.

Even a victory at Mineirao would leave the second-placed side dependent on Flamengo dropping points elsewhere, but that possibility could encourage the visitors to adopt a more adventurous approach as the contest develops.

Cruzeiro will make several changes to the side that defeated Bahia, with Jonathan Jesus and Kaua Moraes unavailable through suspension, while Wesley is also ruled out following a decision by the Superior Court of Sports Justice (STJD).

Bruno Rodrigues will miss the encounter because of contractual restrictions, while Keny Arroyo is unlikely to feature after representing Ecuador during the international break.

There is better news for Artur Jorge, however, as William, Lucas Villalba and Matheus Pereira are available again following their respective suspensions, while Fabricio Bruno has returned to training with the squad and could provide an important defensive boost.

Joao Marcelo, Gabriel Pec and Luis Sinisterra remain in recovery, with Felipe Morais, Kaique Kenji and Ze Lucas still needing further assessments before their availability can be determined.

Palmeiras also have several selection concerns following the international break, with Gustavo Gomez and Mauricio unlikely to return in time for Wednesday's contest.

Agustin Giay, Flaco Lopez and Jhon Arias travelled to Brazil on chartered flights during the early hours of Wednesday and are expected to join the squad directly in Belo Horizonte, although their involvement from the start remains uncertain.

Defensively, Ferreira will be without Joaquin Piquerez, who sustained an injury while representing Uruguay, and Murilo, who continues his recovery from a left thigh problem.

Bruno Fuchs and Alexander Barboza are therefore expected to form the central defensive partnership, with Khellven and Artur providing the options in the full-back positions, although Emiliano Martinez could drop into defence if Ferreira opts for a three-man backline.

Marlon Freitas, Lucas Evangelista and Andreas Pereira are among the midfielders expected to provide the necessary balance, while Ramon Sosa, Vitor Roque and Felipe Anderson are competing for attacking positions.

Flaco Lopez and Jhon Arias could initially be named among the substitutes as Palmeiras look to manage their workload following their late return from international duty.

Otavio; William, Bruno, Villalba, Vina; Romero, Henrique; Gerson, Pereira, Marquinhos; Jorge

Miguel; Khellven, Fuchs, Barboza, Artur; Freitas, Evangelista, Pereira, Anderson; Sosa, Roque

The visitors' demanding schedule and selection problems could prevent them from operating at their usual level, but their ability to exploit spaces in transition should still create opportunities against an ambitious Cruzeiro side.

We expect a closely-contested encounter, with neither team doing quite enough to establish control over the other, and a share of the spoils appears to be the most likely outcome.

#1947. Man United transfer news: USA star speaks on joining Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 18:42

Weston McKennie has suggested that he expects at least one USA player to sign for Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino is currently preparing to take charge of his final match as manager of the USA, who face Haiti in the second leg of their UEFA Nations League quarter-final on Tuesday night.

The manner of the team's 6-0 victory in the first leg highlighted that the Stars and Stripes squad have not downed tools for a manager who is leaving for Old Trafford.

Naturally, a number of American players have been suggested as possible additions by Man United ahead of the winter transfer window, with Pochettino addressing that particular possibility on Monday.

Speaking at a press conference, McKennie has acknowledged that it is realistic to expect one of Pochettino's favourites to join him at the Theatre of Dreams.

The midfielder told reporters: "I think that, obviously, the time Pochettino spent here allowed him to appreciate this squad and see the quality it has to offer.

"And yes, I think it's a possibility. We have a lot of guys on this team who will probably make a move soon or within the next year. So I think the links are somewhat inevitable.

"At the end of the day, though, you never know what's going through a manager's head or what kind of players he's looking for. Still, I think you could see a few of us linked with United, and maybe it will actually happen."

Pochettino is expected to prioritise a centre-back, left-back and forward during the winter transfer window.

Fulham's Antonee Robinson is an obvious candidate to be targeted by United for the left-back role.

Meanwhile, Folarin Balogun could also emerge as an option, with Monaco known to need to raise funds to comply with the relevant financial regulations.

#1944. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1935. Man United transfer news: Red Devils planning second 'raid' on Newcastle after reigniting Lewis Hall interest

By Matt Law | 17 Nov 2026 17:57, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 17:59

Manchester United have reportedly identified Newcastle United's Malick Thiaw as a potential transfer target ahead of the winter market.

The Red Devils have struggled defensively this season, conceding 19 times in their 10 Premier League matches, which is the joint-third worst record in the division.

Man United have not kept a single clean sheet in the Premier League this term, while they have also conceded eight times in their four Champions League matches.

The 20-time English champions want to overhaul their defence next summer, with the futures of Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt all unclear at this stage of proceedings.

It is not unrealistic that as many as five new defenders could join the club in 2027.

The bulk of Man United's transfer business next year will take place at the end of the campaign, but the club are expected to be active during the winter market.

According to TEAMtalk, Newcastle's Thiaw has emerged as a genuine option, with the 25-year-old seen as the ideal fit for Man United.

Red Devils sources allegedly believe that a move for the Germany international in January is possible, and the club are now keeping a close eye on his situation.

Newcastle allegedly value Thiaw in the region of £80m - making a mid-season move difficult - but that price could potentially be negotiated down.

Thiaw arrived at St James' Park from AC Milan in August 2025, and he has represented the Magpies on 64 occasions, scoring five goals and registering two assists in the process.

The defender has now played 44 times in the Premier League, scoring four goals, while he has 25 Champions League appearances under his belt at both Milan and Newcastle.

Thiaw is a 10-time Germany international, meanwhile, and having proved himself in England's top flight, it is not difficult to understand why Man United would be keen.

The Red Devils are also allegedly ready to reignite their interest in Lewis Hall, so it could potentially be a double defensive raid on the Magpies next year.

#1932. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1931. Rayan to Liverpool or Manchester United? How the Brazilian’s style suits both clubs

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:16

Rayan is living a fast-moving career in European football. Signed by Bournemouth in January 2026 after standing out at Vasco da Gama, the Brazilian forward quickly won a place in the Premier League and began attracting the attention of bigger clubs. Liverpool are already monitoring his progress, while a statement has put Manchester United in the conversation: the player revealed that he has always supported the Red Devils because of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Andoni Iraola, who worked with Rayan at Bournemouth, took charge of Liverpool at the start of 2026-27. Manchester United have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, a manager known for developing young attackers and for implementing a high-intensity style. But which of the two clubs would be the better destination for the Brazilian? The answer depends less on Rayan’s personal preference and more on the characteristics that have made him one of the most interesting prospects in Brazilian football.

Bournemouth paid Vasco €35m (about £30m) in January 2026, betting on a 19-year-old forward. Adaptation was quick: Rayan scored five goals and provided two assists in 15 games in the second half of last season.

His profile is different from a traditional winger who relies on short dribbles and quick changes of direction to beat a marker. Rayan is a player of strength and acceleration. When he receives with space, he can carry the ball at speed, protect possession with his body and attack the box with few touches.

In the 2025 Brazilian Serie A, Rayan was the player who finished the most carries with a shot, with 33 occasions. He also scored 14 goals in the league, a number that placed him among the competition’s top scorers. The forward is not just a winger who cuts inside, however. Under Fernando Diniz at Vasco, he was also used centrally, as a centre-forward, and showed an ability to win aerial balls and shield possession with his back to goal. His height and physical strength make it possible to imagine growth in that role, although he still has to improve his control and combination play under pressure.

It is also important to consider what is left to develop. Rayan can still improve the quality of his final pass, his choice of moments to shoot and his involvement in building play. Despite the volume of carries that ended in shots, his creative output was more limited. That helps explain why he still needs an environment that gives him freedom to attack without requiring him to be the main organiser of the attack.

This season, the Brazilian has played ten Premier League games, with one goal and no assists. The output does not match his arrival in England, but Rayan remains a frequent starter and is still adapting to a new manager and a model different from Iraola’s.

Liverpool’s interest strengthened after Iraola’s arrival. The Reds followed the Brazilian closely early in the season and could consider a move in 2027. Iraola knows Rayan’s virtues and limitations. It was under his management that the Brazilian began adapting to the intensity of the Premier League, playing mainly on the right and being given freedom to attack space.

The manager also played a part in the step up of other Bournemouth players, such as Antoine Semenyo, who stood out before moving to Manchester City. Tactically, the combination makes sense. Iraola’s teams usually press high, try to win the ball back in advanced areas and accelerate as soon as they find space. He does not demand that his wingers stay tied to the touchline: they can attack inside, combine with the full-backs and appear in different channels. Rayan could play on the right, cutting inside onto his left foot, but also attack depth and offer a physical threat in transitions.

At Liverpool, that characteristic could be useful. The team has changed in attack: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha offer alternatives, but Rayan would add a different profile, a more powerful forward able to carry the ball at speed and attack the box.

There is one caveat. Liverpool already have quality attacking options. The manager also has to manage a more demanding calendar and a team with title ambitions. Rayan could find a way to play, but would hardly have the same freedom as a young player developing at Bournemouth.

Rayan’s link with Manchester United came to light in an interview with ESPN. The forward said he has always supported the club in England because of Cristiano Ronaldo, his great idol. He also recalled the emotion of playing at Old Trafford and beating the Red Devils 3-0 with Bournemouth in October.

The statement became relevant when United hired Pochettino to try to reorganise a team going through a difficult season. The Argentinian has a track record of developing young players and built his best work in England with intense teams, aggressive in the press and quick in transitions. His most usual model starts from a 4-2-3-1, with wingers who often attack inside spaces and full-backs who push on to give width.

That structure could favour Rayan. Starting from the right, the Brazilian would have freedom to carry towards the box, finish with his left foot and attack the spaces created by team-mates’ movement. High pressing also suits his physical ability, although defensive involvement is still an area he needs to improve.

The problem is competition. United already have Bryan Mbeumo, Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha among their attacking options, plus Benjamin Sesko as a central reference. There is also a developmental question. Pochettino usually demands a lot from his players without the ball and works with coordinated attacking movements. For a forward who still needs to improve decision-making and creation, the environment can be positive but also brings high demands. The Brazilian would need to learn to alternate individual carrying with quick combination play and movement without the ball.

United, on the other hand, could offer room to grow if Pochettino sees Rayan as a medium-term project and not an immediate solution to attacking problems. The Argentinian’s ability to develop young forwards is a point in favour, but the squad already has players in similar roles.

Between the two scenarios, Liverpool appear to offer the clearer fit. Iraola already knows the Brazilian, knows how to use his strength in transitions and has a model that favours attackers able to carry the ball at speed. The departure of Mohamed Salah has also opened space for a reorganisation of the right side, making the position a concrete possibility for Rayan.

Manchester United have the emotional appeal and a manager whose philosophy could match the Brazilian’s characteristics. But the presence of Mbeumo, Amad and Cunha makes the battle for space more complex. To turn admiration for the club into a transfer, Rayan would need to see a clear sporting plan.

At any rate, the moment is still one of development. At 20, the forward does not need to choose immediately between two giants, especially as he has a contract with Bournemouth until 2031 and is still gaining experience in a demanding league. Rayan has the attributes to reach a top-level club, but his next step needs to be defined by the project that best uses his potential. Between his familiarity with Iraola and his identification with United, Liverpool appear to have a tactical advantage.

#1930. GdS: Inacio ‘more than a replacement’ as €40-45m price tag emerges – the situation

Goncalo Inacio’s name is back in the headlines today and AC Milan are very hopeful of securing him in the new year.

Although talk of a striker has dominated headlines recently, neither Gerry Cardinale nor Ruben Amorim have forgotten about the need to sign a defender. In fact, the pair have never stopped considering a January signing in the backline.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A late attempt was made for Inacio in the summer, and Milan have effectively left the deal on hold with the intention of picking it back up at the first possible opportunity.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, via MilanNews, the Portuguese defender is not seen as a replacement. Instead, he’ll be a starter, alongside Strahinja Pavlovic and Mario Gila, and someone who can raise the bar.

Indeed, he’s someone the club wants to bring in as a pillar for the future, and this is why Amorim and Cardinale are desperate to sign him in January. So much so that they’re not put off by the €40-45 million sought by Sporting.

It’s undeniably a high asking price, but it’s consistent with the cost of the profile Amorim seeks. So, they’d be inclined to pay as much to secure their – importantly – shared top target.

#1929. Vitoria vs Bragantino - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 17 Nov 2026 18:17

Vitoria will be looking to end a five-match winless run when they welcome Bragantino to the Estadio Manoel Barradas on Thursday in a Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A encounter.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with 38 points from 34 matches, just one point above the relegation zone, while Braga occupy eighth place with 47 points and are hoping to keep their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Copa Libertadores alive.

Vitoria head into Thursday's encounter under pressure after losing 3-0 at home to Fluminense in their most recent league outing, a result that extended their winless run to five matches.

The Rubro-Negro had previously suffered a 2-0 defeat away to Coritiba, following consecutive 1-1 draws against Athletico Paranaense and Corinthians, while their earlier meeting with Sao Paulo ended in a 2-1 loss.

Their last league victory came on October 8, when they thrashed Chapecoense 4-0 at home, leaving them with only two points from the last five matches, the fewest points by any team in the league in that period.

The defeat to Fluminense also marked a difficult end to Jair Ventura's time in charge, with the coach dismissed after Vitoria slipped to within one point of the relegation zone.

Rafael Lacerda has been appointed and will take charge of his first match on Thursday, having had the international break to work with the squad and prepare for the challenge ahead.

Vitoria's home record offers some encouragement, however, as they have won 10 of their 17 league matches at the Barradao, drawing twice and losing five times, though they are without a win in their last two games as hosts.

Bragantino, meanwhile, arrive in Salvador after recording consecutive victories, having beaten Chapecoense 3-0 before securing a 2-1 home win over Santos in their most recent match.

Massa Bruta took the lead against Santos via an own goal from Rodinei, before conceding an equaliser in the 37th minute, but Wallace Yan scored his third goal in two games to claim all three points.

Vagner Mancini's side have now won three of their last five league matches, drawing once and losing once, with their other victory coming in a 4-2 home success over Cruzeiro, while they recorded a 1-1 draw away to Remo during that period, with their only defeat coming against Palmeiras, who beat them 2-0 in Sao Paulo.

Braga’s away form has been less convincing than their home performances, having won only four of their 17 matches on the road, drawing five and losing eight, while they are without a win in their last eight league games and last 10 across all competitions.

However, the head-to-head record also gives the visitors reason for optimism, having won the last two meetings between the clubs, though the Massa Bruta have lost the last two on the road.

Vitoria will be without several players through injury, including Nathan Mendes, Fabiano Souza, Edu, Camutanga, Ramon and Riccieli, while Dudu is also listed as unavailable.

Luan Candido and Nacho Laquintana are expected to miss out because they are on loan from Bragantino and their agreements reportedly include clauses requiring Vitoria to pay a fee for each player to feature against their parent club.

Emmanuel Britez is available again after serving a suspension, and the defender is expected to partner Caca in central defence.

Lacerda is also likely to retain Lucas Arcanjo in goal, with Rene, Erick and Matheuzinho among the attacking options as he prepares for his first match in charge.

Bragantino will be without Lucas Barbosa, who is suspended, while Rodriguinho and Davi Gomes are sidelined through injury.

Jose Hurtado is also a doubt after picking up a thigh injury, leaving Mancini with some decisions to make in defence as he attempts to maintain his team's recent momentum.

Yan is expected to retain his place in the attacking midfield, while Eduardo Sasha should lead the line.

Arcanjo; Mateusinho, Caca, Brítez, Jamerson; Goncalves, Martinez, Baralhas; Erick, Matheuzinho; Rene

Volpi; Augusto, Marques, Rodríguez, Capixaba; Fabinho, Ramires; Mosquera, Yan, Herrera; Sasha

Lacerda's appointment could provide Vitoria with a lift, especially with the match taking place at the Barradao, where they have won 10 times this season.

However, Bragantino's recent improvement should allow them to compete, and we expect both sides to find the net before sharing the points.

#1928. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1926. Declan Rice’s new five-year deal to 2031 marks his rise from £105m signing to Arsenal leader

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:28

Declan Rice’s new contract with Arsenal recognises a transformation built over three seasons. When he arrived at the Emirates Stadium in July 2023, the midfielder was a high-impact signing: he cost £105m, a record for a British player at the time, and carried the expectation of lifting a team that had just lost the Premier League title to Manchester City.

Today, at 27, Rice is an English champion, one of the leaders of the dressing room and one of the team’s technical reference points. The new five-year deal shows Arsenal’s intention to keep him at the centre of the project through his physical and technical peak. It also reflects his changing status within the club, as Rice is expected to earn a salary close to that of Bukayo Saka, until now the squad’s top earner.

Rice was not just an expensive signing who lived up to expectations. He became a more complete player, widened his influence across different phases of play and took on responsibilities beyond his role in midfield. The promise of 2023 has become one of the faces of a championship team and a leader for the cycle that starts now.

Rice’s arrival came at a decisive moment for Mikel Arteta’s project. In 2022-23, Arsenal spent much of the season at the top but lost steam in the closing stretch and finished five points behind Manchester City. The team had shown that they could compete for the title, but they needed more quality, depth and experience to sustain a challenge to the end.

Rice had characteristics that answered several of those needs. At 24, he was already West Ham United’s captain, had experience with England and had just won the Conference League. Arsenal beat the competition and completed the signing for £100m fixed plus £5m in bonuses.

The fee raised expectations. It was not enough for Rice to be a good holding midfielder: he had to justify a historic investment and help Arsenal take the step needed to compete with City. His first season showed the scale of the signing quickly.

Rice played 38 Premier League games, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists. The number of goal contributions was a considerable improvement on his West Ham record, but his impact was not limited to attacking output. Arsenal again finished as runners-up, but Rice had already become one of the team’s most important players. The signing did not deliver an immediate title, but it helped turn expectation into a conviction that the club had found a midfielder able to carry their project for many years.

Rice’s development also reflects the way Arteta changed his use. Early in his time at Arsenal, the Englishman often played as the deepest midfielder, responsible for protecting the defence and offering a reference point for build-up. It was a familiar role, close to the one he had at West Ham, but it did not use his full repertoire.

After an adaptation period, especially from the start of 2024, Arteta began using him more often as a box-to-box midfielder on the left. The change let Rice use one of his main qualities: carrying the ball at speed, breaking lines and arriving in the opposition area while still contributing to defensive recovery.

The Englishman gained more freedom to attack space, appear at the edge of the box and join attacking combinations. His physical power became a weapon for taking Arsenal into the opposition half, while his ability to get back helped keep balance when the team lost the ball. Instead of just protecting team-mates, Rice also began to drive the team.

Set pieces were another important tool. Rice began taking corners and free-kicks, using the accuracy of his delivery and his ability to put the ball in dangerous areas. Since his arrival, he has provided ten assists from set pieces in the Premier League. His two free-kick goals against Real Madrid in the 2024-25 Champions League quarter-finals were the most emblematic moment of that evolution.

Versatility does not mean Rice has no fixed position or needs to take part in every attacking action. The most recent development lies in choosing moments. With Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard offering different partnership options, Arteta has alternated the height at which the Englishman receives the ball and the freedom he has to advance.

The ability to perform different roles is one of the reasons Rice has become so important to Arteta. In the title-winning season, he was used both as the most advanced midfielder and in a midfield pair alongside Zubimendi. He is not just a player who adapts to different positions: he lets the manager change the structure of the team without necessarily changing personnel.

Rice’s growth was not only tactical. Over the seasons, he also became one of the squad’s main voices. His direct personality, willingness to demand more from team-mates and ability to take responsibility in difficult moments made him a reference point for the group.

One example came in April, when Odegaard was out injured and Rice was given the captain’s armband. He had worn it on other occasions, but the choice reinforced a perception that had been building: his influence does not depend on being the official captain.

In Arsenal’s 2025-26 Premier League title, which ended a 22-year wait for the competition, Rice was one of the protagonists of the campaign, with 36 appearances, four goals and five assists in the league. More than his statistical contribution, his ability to maintain intensity in different roles was fundamental.

Declan Rice at Arsenal - all competitions since joining in July 2023 2023-24: 51 games, 48 starts, 33 wins, 8 draws, 10 defeats, 7 goals, 9 assists (64.7% wins) 2024-25: 52 games, 48 starts, 28 wins, 16 draws, 8 defeats, 9 goals, 10 assists (53.8% wins) 2025-26: 55 games, 49 starts, 37 wins, 12 draws, 6 defeats, 5 goals, 9 assists (67.3% wins) 2026-27 (in progress): 15 games, 14 starts, 13 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat, 1 goal, 5 assists (86.7% wins) Total: 173 games, 159 starts, 111 wins, 37 draws, 25 defeats, 22 goals, 33 assists (64.2% wins)

Trophies for Arsenal (3): Premier League 2025-26, Community Shield 2023, Community Shield 2026

Official matches only (Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, EFL Cup and Community Shield). Matches decided on penalties count as draws. Data up to 16 November 2026. Sources: FBref (Opta data), BeSoccer and Opta Analyst.

The challenge now is to sustain this level without ignoring fatigue. Rice has come from seasons with a high volume of games, often exceeding 50 matches for club and country. Last season, he played 54 games for Arsenal in all competitions, in addition to England commitments. Managing his workload will be important for him to keep his influence over a demanding calendar.

By extending his contract to 2031, Arsenal secure a player who still has years at his peak ahead and who already knows Arteta’s demands in depth. The club no longer need to wait for Rice to become a leader: that stage has already happened. Now the expectation is that he helps lead the next chapters of a project that intends to keep competing for the main trophies.

#1925. Former SPFL starlet’s wonder strike seals stunning promotion with ex-Rangers icon in the dugout

Former Airdrieonians midfielder Justin Devenny was the hero for Northern Ireland as his wonder strike in the 1-1 draw with Hungary sealed their shock promotion to League A of the Nations League at the Puskas Arena.

Managed on the touchline by former Rangers hero Steven Davis in Budapest, the 41-year-old stepped into the head coach role on a crucial night for Northern Ireland, with manager Michael O’Neill suspended and forced to watch from the stands.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Promoted to League B during their last Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland entered Tuesday night’s game in remarkable form. Top of the group ahead of kick-off, they’d won three and drawn two, without conceding a single goal.

Requiring just a draw against Hungary to seal back-to-back Nations League promotion, they came under heavy pressure in the opening stages, with the home side finally breaking Northern Ireland’s resistance in the 35th minute when Barnabas Varga capitalised on a mistake from Trai Hume to place beyond Pierce Charles as the visitors conceded for the first time in 500 minutes.

Northern Ireland players vigorously appealed for a penalty after Ciaron Brown went down under a challenge from Andras Schafer in the area in the build-up to the goal, with Hungary’s subsequent clearance directly leading to Varga’s opener. However, referee Marco Guida waved away protests following a VAR check.

Searching for the goal that would secure a first promotion to League A, Northern Ireland battled back after the restart and thought they’d levelled when Isaac Price cannoned a long-range effort off the post just after the hour mark.

They found their equaliser shortly afterwards, though, and it was definitely worth the wait. A long throw from Sunderland defender Hume was half-cleared by the Hungarian defence before falling to Devenny, who took a deft first touch to control the ball, before flicking it up and blasting a volley into the top corner.

Despite being born in Irvine, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Northern Ireland due to his grandparents. Devenny told the Belfast Telegraph that he opted to represent Northern Ireland after they approached him first and showed genuine faith in his abilities before Scotland did. During the interview, he emphasized that he chose to play for the nation he felt actively wanted him.

He began his career in the Kilmarnock youth system and spent time on loan with Broomhill and Airdrieonians before signing for the Diamonds on a permanent deal in the summer of 2022. His impressive form in the Scottish Championship won him a shock move to the English Premier League with Crystal Palace just 12 months later.

Playing over 50 games for the Eagles, the versatile midfielder won the Conference League, the FA Cup and the Community Shield during his time at Selhurst Park, before moving to EFL Championship side Stoke City for an undisclosed fee on deadline day. Scoring a brace on his debut for the club in a 4–0 win over Charlton Athletic, he’s been a regular for the Potters as they chase promotion to the top flight.

As a result, he will not return until the final round, against Sao Paulo at the Arena da Baixada. Jorge Rivaldo and Renan Peixoto are the natural options given their profile, but manager Odair Hellmann could also opt to use forward Kerwin Vargas in an adapted role.

In the same hearing, the Parana side were also punished. The fine for racist gestures attributed to a fan during the match against Vasco was increased to R$30,000 (approximately £4,200). The decision was taken by a majority of votes.

Currently fifth with 54 points, Athletico could close the gap on Fluminense, who occupy the final Libertadores spot. Bahia and Atletico Mineiro, however, are also in the same points range.

In a late development, Gonzalo Plata was released from the Ecuador squad for “personal reasons” and could become an unexpected boost. Having played just 13 minutes against Costa Rica, he should not, in theory, show any physical wear.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remain with their national teams and are not expected to return in time.

On the medical front, experienced left-back Alex Sandro has recovered from muscular oedema in his left thigh and has returned to training with the group, although Ayrton Lucas is expected to be the first choice for Portuguese manager Leonardo Jardim.

Midfielder Lucas Paqueta has not yet fully recovered from a knee problem sustained during the thrashing of Vasco, so he is unlikely to be included without a reasonable amount of training, according to Jardim himself. Danilo, meanwhile, continues his recovery schedule following a jaw fracture and also remains sidelined.

The point of concern is the number of players one booking away from suspension: Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Erick Pulgar, Arrascaeta, Pedro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Should any of them be booked by referee Rafael Klein, they would miss the clash against Palmeiras in the following round.

Besides Viveros, Dantas is also serving a suspension due to the automatic one-match ban for a third yellow card. Young centre-back Arthur Dias, who is attracting interest from several European clubs, is another absentee. He is set to play for the Brazil national team against Singapore and is not expected to return to Brazil in time.

Defender Lucas Esquivel is still recovering from a hip injury and will be assessed on matchday, but he is expected to complete the back line alongside Gaston Benavidez and Juan Aguirre. Goalkeeper Santos and Bruno Zapelli could be given a chance in the starting eleven.

Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Pereira, Leo Ortiz, Ayrton Lucas; Pulgar, Jorginho, Arrascaeta; Carrascal, Pedro, Samuel Lino. Manager: Leonardo Jardim.

Athletico Paranaense possible starting lineup:

Santos; Benavidez, Aguirre, Esquivel; Gilberto, Luiz Gustavo, Jadson, Mendoza; Bruno Zapelli, Joao Cruz, Kerwin Vargas. Manager: Odair Hellmann.

Athletico's task would have been difficult enough as it is, but with their top scorer and best defender both unavailable, it is hard to see the visitors taking anything from this encounter.

For Flamengo, the priority will be to maintain their formidable home record and head into the most eagerly anticipated game of the year in a favourable position. A convincing victory at the Maracana would be the ideal way to achieve that.
