#1919. Scotland best and worst case Euro 2028 qualifying draw scenarios as seeding pots confirmed

Scotland's potential qualification opponents for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - have been finalised following the conclusion of the Nations League group stage.

Seeding pots for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6, were based solely on the performance of each team in the Nations League across the 2026 campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sebastien Pocognoli's men have been placed in Pot 3 due to finishing third in Group B1 after taking seven points from a possible 18 in an underwhelming start to life under the Belgian head coach.

Scotland finished nine points behind group winners Switzerland, who put seven goals past them without reply over two matches, and four points behind runners-up Slovenia, who also won at Hampden after a goalless draw in Ljubjlana. North Macedonia, who Scotland defeated home and away, finished bottom of the group on zero points.

Attention now turns to the Euro 2028 qualifiers, which will feature six groups of four and six groups of five. The five-team groups will begin their qualification campaign in March 2027 while the groups of four will not start until September 2027.

If Scotland are drawn into a group of four they will face a 10-month wait for their next competitive fixture with friendlies required to fill the empty calendar for March and June next year.

However, Scotland are more likely to be drawn into a group of five due to Uefa tilting the odds in favour of teams who are not involved in any Nations League play-offs or quarter-finals in March.

This would see Scotland play eight qualifiers instead of six, kicking off in March with further games in June, September/October and November.

Scotland cannot be drawn in a group with their co-hosts England, Wales or Republic of Ireland. While Northern Ireland are no longer staging tournament matches after Casement Park was dropped from the bid, they retain a special status in the qualifying draw and will also be kept apart from the co-hosts.

Scotland will draw one team each from Pots 1, 2, and 4, plus one team from Pot 5 if placed into one of the six five-team groups.

Here are the confirmed seeding pots and possible opponents for Scotland:

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain. (England excluded).

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey. (Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Wales excluded).

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta.

A dream draw for Scotland would involve facing the lowest ranked nations from each pot. Such a group would involve Greece, Bosnia & Herzegovina, San Marino and Gibraltar.

Another more favourable draw would pair Scotland with Denmark, Czechia, Moldova and Liechtenstein.

The nightmare scenario for Scotland would be drawing the highest ranked nation from each pot, which would involve matches against Spain, Switzerland, Finland and Azerbaijan.

Another more difficult draw would involve Scotland facing France, Austria, Bulgaria and Lithuania.

To qualify automatically for Euro 2028 Scotland must finish as one of the 12 group winners or eight best runners-up. The other four group runners-up enter the play-offs.

There is, however, a potential safety net for Scotland with Uefa reserving two spots for co-hosts who do not achieve qualification on the pitch. Assuming England as pot one seeds qualify, Scotland will be competing with Wales and Republic of Ireland to get in through the back door.

If two co-hosts qualify on the pitch, then Scotland and the other co-host who fail to qualify would automatically take advantage of the safety net.

The only scenario where Scotland would fail to make it to Euro 2028 via the safety net is if three co-hosts fail to qualify and Scotland's qualification record is the worst of the trio.

Scotland are only guaranteed to play Euro 2028 matches at Hampden if they qualify the proper way. Using the safety net opens the door to potentially playing their matches elsewhere.

Dundee have paid tribute to one of their all-time greats following the death of Bobby Wilson at the age of 83.

A member of the club's Hall of Fame, the right-back played 411 times for the Dark Blues across 11 seasons after joining from Cowdenbeath in 1966 and lifted the League Cup in 1973.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He still holds the club record for most European appearances (17) and was a key part of the Dundee side that reached the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup semi-finals in 1968, losing to Don Revie's Leeds.

Wilson scored Dundee's only goal in the tie, an equaliser in the 1-1 first leg draw at Dens Park, before Bobby Ancell's side went down to a 1-0 defeat in the second leg at Elland Road.

He was also part of Dundee's last major trophy success, which was achieved in 1973 with a 1-0 win over Celtic in the final of the League Cup. Wilson provided the delivery for Gordon Wallace to score the only goal.

Wilson was inducted into Dundee's Hall of Fame in 2013 on the 40th anniversary of that victory.

After leaving Dens Park, he managed Raith Rovers as well as Highland League sides Lossiemouth and Keith before a 10-year tenure at Ross County, overseeing their entry to the Scottish League in 1994.

"Everyone at the club sends their condolences to Bobby's family and friends at this very difficult time," said a Dundee statement. "Comfortably in the top 10 of most appearances for the club, Bobby retains a place in the hearts of Dundee fans as a member of the last team to bring silverware back to Dens."

Ross County also paid tribute in a statement which read: "We are deeply saddened by the passing of our former manager, Bobby Wilson, whose leadership and dedication played a key role in transforming the club during our Highland League days and gaining entry into the Scottish Football League.

"His commitment and passion will never be forgotten, and his legacy will live on in the hearts of everyone connected to the club. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time."

#1913. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1912. CM: Krösche given ‘no limits’ for January as Cardinale prepares €100m budget

AC Milan are going to have a big January and Markus Krösche has been given his brief by Gerry Cardinale, it seems.

After a solid start to the season, Cardinale plans to invest more in Ruben Amorim and he will do so at the first opportunity, in January. So, alongside making his new Director of Football hire, he will invest heavily in the mercato.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to Calciomercato.com, Krösche will be given ‘no limits’ by Cardinale when he steps into his role in the new year. The German will be given a substantial budget to help transform the squad in the mercato and this has also been made clear to his staff already at the club.

€70 million has already been put aside for a striker, with two huge names linked. Then, another €30m will be made available for other positions. There are, as the report writes, another two or three priority moves that need to be completed, too.

A full-back and a winger are desired, but the second priority will be a central defender. Goncalo Inacio is the main target and he’s set to cost between €40-45m. In short, it’s going to be a big month for the incomings.

However, Krösche’s main task will be sorting the outgoings. Cardinale hopes that the German will be able to sell a few players who haven’t convinced this season to help make funds available. Additionally, he will be responsible for sorting out the futures of Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto.

#1911. ‘Exceptional’ - Former Leeds and Man City man shares bold Brighton and Arsenal title prediction

Former Leeds United man Danny Mills believes 'exceptional' Brighton can achieve Champions League football this season.

The Seagulls have emerged as surprise title contenders this term and are currently second, five points adrift of leaders Arsenals.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton are the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals from 10 matches. They have also been impressive at the back with seven clean sheets from 10 matches.

Mills, speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds, said: "Brighton would need a little bit of luck, possibly with injuries. We've seen Leicester do it in the past.

"Are they likely to win it? Probably not. But is Europa League or Champions League football a possibility with the league the way it is in flux at the moment. Absolutely.

"[Brighton] are incredibly well coached. If you listen to some of the best players that I've ever been around, the likes of Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, that have seen these up first hand and seen some of the coaching that Fabian Hurzeler is doing, it's exceptional.

"It's clear, it's concise, they have a specific plan that they work to, and it's working for them. I think they will keep it up but they will be tested at some point.

"Undoubtedly there will be a dip at some point within that. But at the moment they're playing with great confidence in what they're doing, great confidence and belief in their manager."

Mills was also full of praise for Brighton transfer model and the fact they give new players and youngsters a chance to shine on the biggest stage.

"I think we've seen in recent years the business model has changed somewhat. I think you have to look at it, you know, teams understand now that bringing in young players and making them better, EPPP ripped the heart out of the academy system, really.

“So all the top clubs took all the best young players very, very early and clubs were not getting huge fees for them at that stage. So I think what they're trying to do now is hold on to these players a little bit longer, develop these players, give themselves a chance.

“I think we've seen it across the leagues, that's the model. It's going back to maybe the old days of let's give players an opportunity, let's give them plenty of game time, improve them, and then sell them on and keep doing the same thing.

“It's no different from the Brentford model, the Brighton model. It's exactly what they're doing. So then identification and recruitment in all that is absolutely key.”

#1910. When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, who Scotland could face and when does the campaign start

Scotland will soon discover which opponents they will face as they look to qualify for the third consecutive European Championship under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

Ending a 23-year exile from major tournaments by sealing a spot at Euro 2020 (played in 2021) under former manager Steve Clarke, they repeated the trick three years later, edging out Norway for a spot in the 2024 tournament in Germany.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Now under new boss Pocognoli, a disappointing third-placed finish in the Nations League has made Scotland’s hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - slightly harder after results meant they were placed in Pot 3 of the draw.

Want to know when the draw will take place, how to watch and which teams Scotland could face and which they will avoid? Here is everything you need to know about the Euro 2028 qualifying draw:

The qualifying draw for the European Championships in 2028 will take place in Belfast, Northern Ireland, on Sunday 6 December 2026. The tournament will be co-hosted by the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.

If you want to stream the draw via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and via the official UEFA YouTube channel.

Scotland’s third-placed finish in Nations League Group B1 means they will be placed into Pot 3 of the draw next month. They will be drawn against once team each from Pots 1, 2 and 4 and potentially pot 5, depending on if they are placed into one of the six five-team groups.

They can’t be drawn against England, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland or Wales, with UEFA keeping the tournament co-hosts separated in the qualifying phase of Euro 2028.

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain.

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkiye.

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

The Euro 2028 qualifiers begin in March 2027, but Scotland’s campaign will depend entirely on the outcome of the qualifying draw in December.

As attested to above, Scotland will be placed into either a four-team or five-team group. If they are drawn in a four team group, fixtures will begin in March 2027. However, should they be drawn in a five team group, their first Euro 2028 qualifying fixture will take place in September 2027.

#1909. Tottenham urged to sign £12.5m midfielder who would be "top five" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 20:21

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to make an approach for AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana, who could be one of the "top five" players in his position in the Premier League.

The Lilywhites spent big to reinforce their engine room during the summer with the signings of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes for a combined £185m, while Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Bergvall and Conor Gallagher remain on the books too.

However, a report from Italian outlet Calciomercato states that Tottenham are 'ready to attack' for Fofana, who is currently on loan at Sevilla from Milan and has made a positive impression in La Liga.

Fofana has scored one goal and provided three assists in nine Spanish top-flight appearances, but he is only under contract with Milan until 2028, and his long-term future remains unclear.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, former Milan striker Mark Hateley implored Tottenham to make a move for Fofana, whom he believes everyone would be casting their eye on if he became available.

"That's the type of player all top clubs would look for, even as a bit-part player," Hateley said. "He's one of those players who'll get into the side and be good in it, and then out of the side if need be.

“There are a lot better players out there, but he is a good player. That's the difference between the top three, four, five clubs now. You can pay £50m or £60m for a guy who's just going to be knocking around the squad, and that's where we are in the football world right now.

“He'd be one of the top three, four or five in England anyway; we'd all be looking at that sort of player if he became available.

“Spurs are still struggling to find something at the moment. It's normally the player you never imagine is going to make everybody else work: the squad player, your £30m or £40m, maybe £50m player, and it works.

“That's where we are with Tottenham right now. I've seen them play very well this season, but I've also seen them play very, very poorly, and that's the frustration with supporters, because you don't know which team is going to turn up. It's not an 11 you're building right now, it's an 18 or 19-man starting line-up."

Reportedly valued at just £12.5m by AC Milan, Fofana does not trump his Spurs rivals in many statistical columns, but the 27-year-old is superior to Fernandes, Tonali, Gallagher and Bentancur on a few metrics.

Fofana's 0.38 assists per 90 minutes is the highest total among the quintet, as is his 1.15 successful dribbles per game, from 3.56 attempts; Gallagher is second in the latter statistic with 1.42.

Fofana has also been dispossessed on the fewest occasions - just 0.76 times per 90 minutes - and was no stranger to a direct involvement during his first two seasons with Milan.

The ex-Monaco man has scored three goals and set up 13 more in 88 games for the Rossoneri, although he was left out of France's World Cup squad and has not represented Les Bleus since 2024.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.Bet.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He leaves his position as assistant manager and head of football operations at league leaders Stranraer to join a team six places further down the table.

Fellows spent almost 10 years with East Kilbride, were he started as a teenage kit boy, working his way up to interim manager in 2023, and winning the Lowland League Cup during a two-month spell in charge.

He has a day job in office furniture sales and holds a Uefa A licence.

"You have to earn people's respect as a person," Fellowes told BBC Scotland. "When you are a young guy and you're leading a football club, I don't think you can come in and change everything and lead with an iron fist.

"You have to get people's respect on and off the pitch. I know there will be plenty of criticism and there will be plenty of people sitting here today doubting that I'm capable of doing this job at 28.

"But now really the work for me has started on, by the end of the process, having gained those people onside to say, 'he was more than capable of doing this job and we're delighted to have him here'.

"I can only do that through winning games of football."

Fellowes claims the mantle of Scottish football’s youngest ever head coach from Jim Duffy, who was 29 when he took charge of Falkirk in 1988, while Rhys McCabe was appointed player/manager of Airdrieonians at the same age four years ago.

Former St Mirren and Clyde manager Danny Lennon, now Dumbarton director of football, revealed age was not a factor when considering who to appoint as a replacement for Frank McKeown, who was sacked last month.

“What really impressed us about Martin was his football knowledge, the clarity of his coaching philosophy, his understanding of player development and the passion and ambition he has for the game,” Lennon said.

“Throughout our conversations, Martin demonstrated a real understanding of how he wants his teams to play, the standards he expects and how he intends to help players improve, both individually and collectively.

“He is a young and ambitious coach who has worked extremely hard to develop his knowledge and prepare himself for an opportunity as a head coach in the SPFL. I believe football should always be about recognising ability and potential, regardless of age or background.

“Martin has earned this opportunity through the commitment he’s shown to his development and the qualities he’s demonstrated throughout the recruitment process. We fully appreciate that managing at this level comes with challenges, and it’s important that we provide him with the right environment and support to succeed.

“We have a group of players who have shown a genuine willingness to learn and improve, and we’re excited about the opportunity to continue that development under Martin’s leadership.

“Our ambitions remain clear. We want to improve performances, compete towards the top end of the league and establish a strong football identity that our supporters can be proud of.

“This appointment is about both the present and the future of Dumbarton Football Club. We’re looking forward to working closely with Martin, supporting his development as a manager and, most importantly, helping him bring success to the club.

“I’d ask our supporters to get right behind Martin and the team as we begin this next chapter together.”

#1903. Wayne Rooney opens up on mental health struggles, drinking and seeking help from a therapist

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:39

Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide during his time at Manchester United. The former England captain, 41, spoke about it on the Life at the Midpoint podcast, hosted by Gabby Logan, describing a period when his eldest son Kai was still a baby. The interview was reported by the BBC and also picked up by Sky Sports.

‘I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide,’ Rooney said. ‘You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.’

Rooney was speaking about years when he was at his best on the pitch. According to the BBC, Kai is now 17, so the period was roughly 17 years ago. He describes it as a time when he had just got married and just had a son.

‘It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t,’ he said. Asked by Logan about the hardest moment of his life, he said that when he was drinking he would shut himself at home for two days and just drink, at what was probably the best phase of his career in playing terms.

He joined United from Everton in 2004 and, according to the BBC, became the club’s all-time top scorer with 253 goals in 559 games. He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Europa League, the FA Cup and three League Cups before returning to Everton in 2017. He remains a legend at Old Trafford, where Mauricio Pochettino is now beginning his time as boss.

‘I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, I really struggled with it,’ he said on the podcast.

Rooney also explained why nothing showed on the outside at the time. ‘You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,’ he said. He said a feeling that he would be less of a man stopped him admitting his own state. In the end he confided in his wife Coleen and his mother and started speaking to a therapist. He now describes his behaviour at the time as selfish. ‘Coleen helped me enormously,’ he added. ‘She could have left, it was that bad, but she stayed by me and helped me get through it.’

This is not the first time Rooney has spoken about a dark period. In February 2022, when the Rooney documentary came out on Amazon Prime Video and he was managing Derby County, he told the PA news agency, as reported by The42, that he suffered inside for a long part of his career and that a lot of it ended in drinking. He also told the Mail on Sunday, as reported by Inside World Football, that in his early years at United, until about the birth of Kai, he would shut himself at home and drink. He pointed to the pressure of playing for England and United and what the newspapers wrote about his private life. According to PA, he saw a psychologist only briefly at the time.

The new interview is a significant step on from those earlier accounts. In the 2022 pieces, the subjects were alcohol and the pressure of fame, with no mention of suicidal thoughts. Rooney did, however, explain then why he stayed silent as a player. He said he could not go to older players such as Roy Keane or Ryan Giggs and say there was a problem. He added that today it is much easier, because mental health is talked about and problems are caught earlier, especially among young players.

England’s most famous striker of his generation could not speak about his state while he was playing, and speaks most openly about it as a former player and television pundit. He has been named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and currently appears in the ITV reality show I’m a Celebrity. The subject has remained relevant in dressing rooms, as goalkeeper James Trafford showed recently when he left Manchester City over his mental health.

If you or someone you know is struggling, support is available. In the UK, Samaritans can be called free at any time on 116 123.

A five-goal second half blitz underlined the Sports' superior status - but only after the Golds had turned around at half-time at 1-1 and with a glint of an upset in the gleaming, rain-soaked Priory Lane stadium.

George Gaskin and Mitch Hand's squad had made the long trek along the Sussex coast against the background of a frankly awful season so far. They’re a step lower than the Sports, but actually 44 places lower in terms of current league tables.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And if it is ever possible to draw comfort from a 6-1 defeat, they can be satisfied this was a well contested game - which also banished memories of the two clubs' last encounter, an ill-tempered Senior Cup semi-final two seasons ago at Lancing.

Borough had thrown open the gates with free admission at the Connect Management Stadium - and those local football addicts who chose live footy ahead of a warm fireside were actually rather well rewarded.

Steve King's squad is strong on paper but stretched by injuries; but his line-up gave a starting shirt to FA Trophy hero Tyano Wilson as well as young reserve keeper Myles Watkins, and a place on the bench for patient striker Zack Tarrant - who would have the last word of the night.

Wilson created an early chance out of nothing, but his low cross flashed across goal with nobody able to convert. But on just seven minutes, the Sports were ahead: Arthur Grout played a perfectly weighted lofted pass to Liam Nash, who finished in style.

Cue a cascade of goals, through the silvery curtain of drizzle under gleaming lights? Nope - or at least not yet. Littlehampton kept their nerve, had a reasonable share of possession and kept their shape.

And, as the minutes drizzled away, half-time was suddenly approaching with the 1-0 scoreline unchanged. And just as suddenly, the Golds grabbed an equaliser through Marcel Powell - smartly taken if only just deserved on the balance of play.

With dressing room doors slammed tightly shut, King and his staff must have passed a few words of wisdom, and the second half saw a more determined and purposeful home performance.

In fact, it took just two minutes from the restart for Max Sheaf to restore the Sports' advantage with a beauty of a strike - and that set the second-half agenda.

Within five minutes, Myles-Watkins produced a strong save at his near post to deny Powell an equaliser. Then Gold Omotayo tucked one under the keeper to extend the home side's lead, or so they thought - but an offside flag chalked it off. No matter: Borough were now controlling most of the play.

Just past the hour, Laleye and Wilson combined beautifully at pace, to set up Gold's tap-in for 3-1. And three minutes later Owen Bellamy - often an unsung hero in the red Borough shirt - curled in the sweetest of strikes from 25 yards, to put the game effectively beyond Littlehampton's reach.

There was still time for Borough's strikers of the future to make their mark. Tarik Kadric and Tarrant enjoyed space against an understandably tiring visiting defence, and after Omotayo had converted a penalty for handball - furiously disputed by the visitors - it was Tarrant who claimed the final goal.

The tall youngster had too much pace for the Golds defence and his strike cannoned in off the underside of the bar.

For Littlehampton, a long and weary drive home, and that ever-ironic agenda to ‘concentrate on the league’. For the Sports, yet another victory - 20 in 22 games - and the ride rolls on.

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

#1899. Winless run drags on for Burgess Hill Town – and they need an upturn

On Saturday, Gary Mansell’s side conceded three goals in five minutes in a 3-0 defeat at Dover Athletic to exit the FA Trophy at the second-round stage.

And in midweek they slipped to another Isthmian Premier defeat, when a first-half goal by Alfie Cerulli was enough to give Brentwood a 1-0 win at Leylands Park.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Hillians have fallen to 13th in the table and have gone seven games without a win.

They need an improvement soon and will hope to kick-start a revival when they visit Stanway Rovers for a league game on Saturday. They also visit Crowborough in the Velocity Trophy next Tuesday.

Mansell is hopeful that boosts to the squad in the form of the permanent signing of striker George Vorster and the return from injury of other key players will help breathe new life into the season.

At Dover in Saturday’s Trophy tie, three goals in a devastating five-minute spell in the first half proved decisive.

The Hillians made a positive start and Ben Pope threatened early on before a later effort came back off the post.

But Dover took the lead in the 23rd minute through Jack Bates and two minutes later Dequane Wilson-Braithwaite doubled their advantage.

When Corie Andrews added a third in the 27th minute, it felt like game over.

Hill did keep battling away and created chances to get back in it through Chris Whelpdale and Vorster – who the club are delighted to tie into a permanent contract.

Despite the disappointing result, the Hillians’ determination and effort throughout the Trophy tie could not be faulted.

Mansell said afterwards: “For 20 minutes I thought we were the better team. We had a clear game-plan that the boys executed. And we imploded for four minutes and that was game over.

“We were doing well then decided to go off-script and play central passes that weren’t really on. We got beaten in transition three times and they scored three goals – they were ruthless. That cost us the game.

“In the second half we were much better and had a go.”

Mansell said he was delighted goal ace Vorster was now a Hill player, not on loan, and thanked his previous club Slough for helping get the move sealed.

And the manager said he was confident that with the way they were playing and injured personnel like Reggie Ward and Martyn Box coming back in, wins would follow.

#1898. Naivety cost us two points at Scunthorpe: Meeney’s verdict after Worthing’s late heartache

The Rebels looked on course for another notable away National League win when they led 1-0 at Glanford Park courtesy of Jordan Young’s fine finish in the first half.

But the Iron levelled three minutes into time added on, leaving bosses frustrated, with Adam Hinshelwood shown a red card at full-time.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Worthing were denied the chance of a quick return to winning form when Tuesday night’s Sussex Transport Senior Cup tie at Wick was rained off. Now the seventh-placed Reds tackle another double-game week in the league – at home to Harrogate on Saturday and away to Woking on Tuesday.

Assistant boss Jon Meeney told club media after Saturday’s draw: “It was a really good first half away from home – the lads carried out everything we desired.

"But we showed our naivety in the second half and made it a lot harder than it needed to be, hence why we conceded a late goal.

“First half we were present in duels… dealt with their direct balls and showed a real intensity against the ball.

"We passed the ball and got up the pitch to suffocate the opposition at times.

"But we stopped playing and stopped finding solutions in the second half. We lost a bit of bravery and went longer and the game opened up.

"We didn’t arrive on enough second balls, we were disconnected, which gave them space – and that’s the naivety of the group, and you’re going to get that with a young group.

"We’ve got to learn and we’ve got to be better at seeing out games of football in that manner.”

Meeney praised scorer Jordan Young, saying: “We know he can be a game-changer.

"He creates but what we like about Youngy is we know he has that quality and it’s what he does off the ball.”

He said the whole squad needed to learn the off-the-ball side of the game from the likes of Young. Meeney said there was a lot to like about the team’s overall display: “The lads have shown an honest performance, they’ve shown grit and determination, honesty to defend the box, stopping crosses, marking in the box.”

The assistant boss described Worthing’s travelling support as ‘outstanding’ and added: “They were with the boys from minute one. It was a fantastic showing after the game applauding the boys off, and vice-versa.

"But we’re just really disappointed it was a draw – it should have been a win."

#1897. Thomas Tuchel speaks out on James Trafford vs Jordan Pickford battle for England spot

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

‘There’s no number one,’ said the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

#1896. Arsenal lock down defence as Hincapie joins Rice and Raya in contract talks

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:53

Arsenal are in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a new contract, according to the BBC, despite the defender having more than four years left on his current deal. The Ecuador international, 24, is the third key player to be tied down in a single week after Declan Rice and David Raya. BBC football correspondent Sami Mokbel says he is set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms even if he is strongly linked to Barcelona in the last weeks.

On Monday evening, Sky Sports News reported that Rice, 27, had verbally agreed a new deal with Arsenal. On Tuesday morning, Sky Sports, citing The Athletic, reported in its live coverage that goalkeeper Raya, 31, had also agreed a new long-term contract. His current deal runs to 2028, and the Spaniard has won the last three Premier League Golden Gloves, according to Sky. The report came shortly after Raya admitted he would one day like to play in La Liga.

Arsenal have not officially announced any of the agreements, but the BBC says the club are preparing to confirm new contracts for Rice, Raya and Jurrien Timber. Riccardo Calafiori, 24, is also next in line, according to the BBC. The Italian left-back, who joined from Bologna in 2024, has a contract until the summer of 2029, and the club want to begin talks with him in the not-too-distant future.

Hincapie joined on 1 September 2025 from Bayer Leverkusen on a season-long loan with an option. The BBC reported at the time that Arsenal had agreed a £45m fee for a permanent deal, and saw the Ecuadorian as a direct replacement for Jakub Kiwior, who left on loan for Porto. Boss Mikel Arteta introduced him on the club website, saying: ‘Piero is physically really impressive, and his versatility and tactical flexibility give us strong options in defence.’

On 25 June 2026, the club announced they had exercised the option and the move became permanent from 1 July, without disclosing the fee. According to Arsenal, Hincapie made 39 appearances in all competitions in the title-winning season, was the club’s player of the month in February and April, and scored his only goal in February at Wolverhampton Wanderers. The defence he slotted into conceded the fewest Premier League goals for the third season running, according to the club.

The BBC now gives 47 appearances for Arsenal in total, which suggests he has added eight this season. One of them was the November game in Prague, where Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1.

The Hincapie deal is not a protection against losing him for free, as that risk does not exist with more than four years remaining. A one-year extension on better terms looks mostly a reward and a way of aligning his wages with the role he has in the squad. He has gone within a year from a loan replacement for Kiwior to a player the BBC lists among the key members of Arteta’s squad.

The common thread in all three cases is timing. Rice had 18 months plus an option left, according to Sky, Raya had a deal to 2028 and Hincapie more than four years. Arsenal are not negotiating under pressure from expiring contracts, which sends a clear signal that, after the title, they want to build on the existing core. In Raya’s case there is also a defensive logic, as the goalkeeper himself opened the subject of Spain and a new contract makes such temptations more expensive. If Timber is added, and Calafiori in the coming months, Arteta will have a goalkeeper, three defenders and the driving force of midfield all on new contracts.

#1895. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1893. CM: Milan could compete with Newcastle and Aston Villa for Lille gem Ngoy

There’s no shortage of defenders being linked to AC Milan currently and a new name has been proposed to the club today.

With a desire to add more cover in the defence, Milan are keeping a keen eye on the mercato and several profiles are arising that could be of interest. Of course, there are a few headliners, but there are also some rising talents that could explode at San Siro.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Calciomercato.com write that the Rossoneri are beginning to take an interest in Nathan Ngoy, the Belgian defender who is rapidly progressing. Like Diego Moreira, he also scored his first goal for the Red Devils against Italy and the future looks bright for him.

Said to be following in Vincent Kompany’s footsteps, he’s part of the rebuilding of the Belgian defence and has become a starter since the World Cup.

It’s also a reason why his value has risen so much in recent months; after the summer, he was believed to be worth €20 and €25 million, but he’s now got a valuation of around €40m.

Goncalo Inacio and Virgil van Dijk are the main names for the defence currently. Yet, the links between the Diavolo and Lille could help make a route to Ngoy easier, as could his international teammates who play at San Siro.

Newcastle and Aston Villa are also keen on the young defender, so he’s certainly one to watch in the future and it could be a major coup for Milan.

#1892. Man Utd told Chelsea star would be ‘good signing’ for Mauricio Pochettino

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

#1891. Boars beat Anvils to maintain challenge: Roffey 3 – 1 Crawley Down Gatwick

Having not played at the weekend Roffey went into this game knowing a win would take them back into the play-off places. Callum Chesworth was serving a suspension, but Pat Gibbs was back in the starting line up and Dan Pearse on the bench after injury.

Roffey started well with Bailey Moyo firing over in the first minute. Two minutes later Charlie Gibson burst down the left and set up Moyo but Leather in the visitor’s goal pulled off a smart save. Roffey continued to press and after 15 minutes a well-judged pass from Pat Gibbs put Moyo in on goal, but he decided to square it and unfortunately no-one could get the final touch. Five minutes later Jordan Mase must have thought he had scored when put clear in the box, but Leather manages to tip his effort over the bar.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After weathering the early storm Down started to grow into the game with their dangerous front two of Harley and Leslie. Leslie latched on to a long pass and poked it past Boar’s keeper Charlie Burton, but Gibbs raced back to clear the danger. In their next attack the visitors had the ball in the net, but the assistant’s flag was already up.

Down were seeing much more of the ball now and it took a great tackle from Byron Napper to stop Harley getting through on goal. Strong appeals for a penalty from the men in red were waved away by the referee. To add salt to Down’s wounds, a minute later Roffey took the lead. A fast attack resulted in a free kick that top scorer Mase curled round the wall and in for the opener. The game looked well balanced at the interval, with Roffey having seen enough of their visitor’s threat to know that one goal was probably not going to be enough.

Three minutes after the break and one became two with another cracking finish. Stan Berry got to the byline then cut back and curled the ball inside the far post to double the lead and give the Boars some breathing space. With that extra cushion Roffey began to exert more control and Down old boy Callum Kilkenny raced down the left, but his shot hit the outside of the post. The hosts continued to look for a third and Luke Harrison put in a teasing cross that managed to evade the three on rushing Boars.

Evan Hoarty and Luca Allen replaced Moyo and Berry with 25 minutes remaining then in the seventy second minute Kilkenny looked like he had sealed the game for Roffey. His first shot was blocked but he reacted fastest to bury the rebound. It could have been four five minutes later when a blast from Mase was brilliantly saved by Leather.

Approaching the last Ten minutes and Dan Pearse, Hayden Skerry and Teddy Wood replaced Gibson, Napper and Kilkenny. A good illustration of the quality of the Boars squad. Skerry came close as his and Mase’s efforts were cleared off the line as the Boars still looked hungry. However, it was the visitors who completed the scoring when after a foul from a cross resulted in a penalty from which Will Harley sent Burton the wrong way for a consolation goal.

So, a tricky looking fixture had been negotiated and the three goals and three points took Roffey back up into fourth place in what is becoming a rather congested pack of teams behind leaders Haywards Heath and it is the Blues from Heath that will be visiting this Saturday for what should be an exciting encounter.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson(Pearse), Napper (Wood), Gibbs, Meeres, Caplin, Mase, Berry(Allen), Moyo(Hoarty), Kilkenny(Skerry)
